gloss: to get nervous; to get stage fright

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: あがっていませんでした

definitions.gloss: to get nervous; to get stage fright; to freeze up
definitions.explanation: To become extremely nervous or tense in front of others, especially when speaking publicly, performing, or facing an important situation. The anxiety causes one to lose composure or forget what to say.

examples.japanese: {人前|ひとまえ}であがってしまう。
examples.english: I get nervous in front of people.

examples.japanese: {面接|めんせつ}であがって、うまく{話|はな}せなかった。
examples.english: I got nervous during the interview and couldn't speak well.

examples.japanese: {初|はじ}めての{舞台|ぶたい}ですっかりあがってしまい、セリフを{忘|わす}れた。
examples.english: I completely froze up on my first stage performance and forgot my lines.

notes:
USAGE:
This あがる is distinct from {上|あ}がる (to go up, to rise). When used to mean "get nervous," it is typically written in hiragana. The metaphor comes from blood "rising" to one's head, causing flushing and mental confusion.

Common patterns include あがり{症|しょう} (tendency to get nervous, stage fright as a condition) and あがってしまう (to end up freezing from nerves). Often used with {人前|ひとまえ}で (in front of people) or {本番|ほんばん}で (at the actual performance).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {人前|ひとまえ}であがる (to get nervous in front of people)
- あがり{症|しょう} (stage fright, nervousness as a trait)
- すっかりあがる (to completely freeze up)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {緊張|きんちょう}する: to be tense, nervous — more general term; あがる specifically implies losing composure or being unable to function
